title: Geometry Formula Decision Steps
prompt: Use the same sequence you should use on paper during a timed review set.

steps.title: Identify the target
steps.content: Ask first: **What am I solving for?** Area, perimeter, a missing angle, or a missing side each point to different facts in the figure.

steps.title: Identify the figure
steps.content: Name the shape before computing. A right triangle, rectangle, trapezoid, and circle each bring their own rules and formulas.

steps.title: Extract the givens
steps.content: Mark lengths, right angles, equal sides, parallel sides, or angle relationships. Write a short note for each clue you see.

steps.title: Choose the formula from the clues
steps.content: Pick the formula that matches both the figure and the quantity you need. For example, triangle area needs **base and perpendicular height**, not just any two sides.

steps.title: Substitute and check
steps.content: Substitute carefully, solve, and check whether the unit makes sense. Perimeter should end in linear units, while area should end in square units.

fallback.markdown: Geometry is easier when you use the same sequence every time: identify the target, name the figure, mark the useful givens, choose the matching formula, then substitute and check the unit.
